2609.26634.title: Knowledge Pull Requests for Continual Document Authoring
2609.26634.paper_summary: We introduce Knowledge Pull Requests (KPRs), a framework for continual document authoring that makes each change interpretable. Documents require ongoing revision as new knowledge surfaces from other sources, languages, or times, but existing approaches either edit with no account of what knowledge changed or regenerate from scratch. A KPR integrates new knowledge into a document by extracting claims, filtering and routing them to sections, and flagging conflicts with existing content, producing a ChangeLog that separates what knowledge changes (claim proposal) from how the text changes (document diff). We evaluate KPRs on revising Wikipedia across languages and updating query-driven reports on RAGTIME. KPRs integrate more information and better preserve existing content than rewriting from sources or regenerating from scratch, while adding the most information per token generated. A KPR-revised article also grounds question answering better than a frontier model with search, which does not surface knowledge documented only in other languages.
2609.26634.paper_summary_zh: 我們介紹知識拉取請求（KPRs），這是一個持續文件創作的框架，使每個變更都可解釋。隨著來自其他來源、語言或時間的新知識浮現，文件需要不斷修訂，但現有的方法要麼在不考慮變更知識的情況下進行編輯，要麼從頭開始重新生成。KPR通過提取主張、過濾並將其路由到相應部分，以及標記與現有內容的衝突，將新知識整合到文件中，生成一個變更日誌，將知識變更（主張提案）與文本變更（文件差異）區分開來。我們在跨語言修訂維基百科和更新基於查詢的RAGTIME報告時評估KPRs。KPR比從來源重寫或從頭生成更能整合更多信息並更好地保留現有內容，同時每生成的標記添加的信息最多。KPR修訂的文章在回答問題方面也比帶有搜索的前沿模型更具基礎，因為後者無法顯示僅在其他語言中記錄的知識。
2609.26634.author: Alexander Martin et.al.
